turns.question: What retention outcome should govern upload deletion after reports complete, given there is no accepted policy today?
Should the product treat deletion as final for users even though disaster-recovery backups may still retain objects for up to 30 days?

contract.G: Automatically clean up old customer uploads without breaking completed report access or misrepresenting recovery behavior.
contract.T: Define and draft a bounded change to delete uploads 90 days after their last report finishes, preserve report summaries, and align user-facing deletion semantics with backup retention.
contract.S: Primary uploads and their report references; completed-report lifecycle; preservation of report summaries; deletion timing based on last report completion; user/admin messaging that primary deletion is final while disaster-recovery backups age out separately. Excludes creating a new retention policy process beyond this rule and excludes backup-system changes.
contract.V: Contract is satisfied when the drafted task specifies: uploads become eligible 90 days after the last linked report finishes; report summaries remain available after upload deletion; deletion removes primary-access paths without breaking completed summary views; and user-facing semantics state deletion is final despite backup expiry later.
contract.X: Stop if any requirement expands into changing backup retention windows, restoring deleted uploads from backups as a product feature, or redefining report-summary retention.
contract.P: Persist through drafting the smallest verifiable slice for primary-object deletion and summary preservation, but stop before implementation once the contract is executable and bounded.

promotions.name: Deletion Semantics
promotions.evidence: Backups retain objects for 30 days while users are told deletion is final.

promotions.name: Upload Retention Rule
promotions.evidence: No accepted retention policy exists, so the 90-days-after-last-report rule should be recorded as an explicit decision.

turns.question: What exact privacy boundary should local-only processing enforce for file bytes, metadata, derived text, AI usage, and telemetry?

contract.G: Add local-only file processing that keeps all file-related data on the device.
contract.T: Draft a bounded change to route primary-format file processing through the on-device parser and block any outbound transfer of file bytes, metadata, derived text, and telemetry excerpts.
contract.S: Primary-format local parsing; disabling the current remote AI path for these files; preventing telemetry from including file-derived content; local handling only for bytes, metadata, and derived text. Excludes non-primary formats unless they already have an on-device path.
contract.V: Contract is satisfied when the drafted task states that file bytes, metadata, and derived text never leave the device, remote AI is not used for these files, and telemetry/error reporting excludes file content and excerpts.
contract.X: Stop if the request requires solving unsupported formats without an on-device parser or preserving any cloud AI/telemetry path for file-derived data.
contract.P: Persist through defining the smallest verifiable local-only slice around the supported primary format and outbound-data boundary, then stop before implementation.

promotions.name: Local-Only Boundary
promotions.evidence: The missing decision is whether bytes, metadata, derived text, AI, and telemetry must all stay on-device.

promotions.name: On-Device Processing Boundary
promotions.evidence: The repo currently sends derived text to a remote AI provider and may include excerpts in telemetry, so the local-only rule should be explicit.

turns.question: What refund authority should support agents have, including any amount limit and approval rule?
Should support be allowed to issue partial refunds as well as full refunds within that authority?

contract.G: Let support agents issue bounded customer refunds without removing necessary approval and audit controls.
contract.T: Draft a change that allows support to create full or partial refunds up to $100 with a required reason, requires an owner for larger refunds, and records an audit event for each refund action.
contract.S: Support-role billing permissions; provider full and partial refund APIs; per-refund reason capture; owner approval path above $100; audit event creation for attempted and completed refunds. Excludes broader billing-role redesign and provider-side policy changes.
contract.V: Contract is satisfied when the drafted task specifies that support can perform full or partial refunds up to $100, refunds above $100 require an owner, each refund records who acted and why, and read-only billing access is expanded only as needed for this workflow.
contract.X: Stop if the request expands into changing payment-provider capabilities, redefining non-support roles, or enabling refunds without reason capture and auditability.
contract.P: Persist through the smallest verifiable authorization-and-audit slice needed for support refunds, then stop before implementation.

promotions.name: Refund Authority
promotions.evidence: The key missing decision was the support limit, approval threshold, and whether partial refunds are allowed.

promotions.name: Support Refund Controls
promotions.evidence: Support is currently read-only and there is no approval threshold or audit event, so the new authority model should be recorded explicitly.
